The training setup is also fairly disciplined: reference LLMs are trained under matched budgets on translated data and native baselines, then compared on token efficiency, MT-system choice, benchmark blind spots, and phenomenon-specific Norwegian evaluations.
summary_en.experiments: Four result groups stand out. First is scale and coverage. MultiSynt/MT spans 36 languages and about 4.8T target-language tokens; for many lower- and medium-resource European languages it exceeds the largest comparable open native resource by more than an order of magnitude. Second is pretraining efficiency. On standard multilingual base-model benchmarks, models trained on MultiSynt/MT reach the final score of the HPLT 2.0 native-data baseline using about 72% fewer training tokens, and at a matched 100B-token budget they outperform it by roughly 15% relative. That is a strong indication that translated data can be highly information-dense. Third is evaluation blindness. A fluency-sensitive LLM-as-judge setup cleanly recovers the ranking of translation systems, while standard multiple-choice benchmarks largely fail to separate them. An embedding-space nearest-neighbor analysis further shows that benchmark items tend to sit closer to MultiSynt/MT documents than to HPLT documents, suggesting that benchmark distribution alignment may inflate the apparent strength of translated-data pretraining. Fourth is capability boundary analysis. On Norwegian tasks involving idioms and culturally grounded knowledge, native-data models remain better throughout training. On Norwegian commonsense reasoning, however, translated-data models close the gap and eventually overtake the native baseline. This is one of the most useful findings in the paper because it decomposes the usual criticism of translationese into something operational: translated data is not uniformly worse, but it is weaker on local cultural grounding and idiomatic expression. The overlap experiment between Tower+ 72B and 9B also matters: the downstream gap is small enough that 9B becomes the default production choice, which is relevant for cost-quality trade-offs in large-scale corpus construction.
summary_en.reading_guide: A good reading order is data construction, then training results, then evaluation critique. Start with Section 3. The important parts are not the mechanics of translation at scale but the choices: why Nemotron-CC HQ was used as the source, why the final production pool combines Tower+ with OPUS/HPLT-MT, and why preserving parallel alignment matters for later controlled analysis. Then read Section 4 carefully, since this is where the pretraining value is established. Pay attention to how token efficiency is measured, whether budgets are matched fairly, and how much downstream difference remains between translation systems. After that, read Section 5 with care, because it changes how the earlier gains should be interpreted. Section 5.1 compares LLM-as-judge with standard benchmarks, Section 5.2 gives the embedding-space diagnostic, and Section 5.3 breaks down Norwegian performance into cultural knowledge, idioms, and commonsense. Together they show that benchmark gains should not be read as proof that translated corpora fully replace native corpora. If time is limited, prioritize Figure 1, Figure 3, Figure 6, and the main tables in Sections 4 and 5. Two deeper questions are worth carrying forward: whether the best recipe is a translated-native mixture rather than either source alone, and how multilingual evaluation should separate fluency, cultural grounding, and reasoning instead of collapsing them into a single benchmark score.

recommendation.zh: 应读实验和数据配方；它会改变“翻译语料只能补尾部”的先验，尤其看 100B token matched 对比。
recommendation.en: Read the data recipe and matched-budget results; it weakens the prior that translated corpora are only a tail-language patch.

paper.title: CausalMix: Data Mixture as Causal Inference for Language Model Training
paper.abstract: In Large Language Model (LLM) training, data mixing plays a pivotal role in determining model performance. Recent methods optimize mixture weights via proxy models, but they rely on the assumption of static data distributions. As a result, when the underlying data pool shifts, these methods require costly retraining from scratch. This limitation restricts their ability to scale seamlessly from small settings to larger data pools and model sizes. In this paper, we propose CausalMix to address thi

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文解决的是 SFT 阶段数据配比优化在“数据池会变化”时失效的问题。已有 mixture 优化方法通常把历史训练 run 当成独立样本，直接学习“配比 → 性能”的全局映射，默认最优配比在不同数据池、不同质量状态下大体稳定。作者认为这个假设不成立：同样的数学、代码、指令数据比例，在不同数据质量、难度、风格和复杂度条件下，边际收益会变，甚至会从正迁移变成负迁移。论文要做的是估计一种随数据状态变化的局部因果效应，即在当前数据池状态下，增加某个域的相对占比到底会带来多大收益，而不是记忆一个静态最优配方。
summary.importance: 这是典型的预训练/后训练接口问题，但落点很实：把 data mixture 从经验调参推进到可迁移的状态条件化估计。对基座研究的价值主要有三层。第一，它明确区分了“数据内容本身的状态”和“混合权重”这两个因素，避免把数据质量变化误当成配比规律，这对 pretrain data mixture、curriculum、continual pretrain 都有启发。第二，它试图学习可转移的边际回报，而不是某个固定数据池上的最优点，因此更接近真正可扩展的 recipe 学习。第三，论文给出了可解释的 CATE 分析，揭示 factual knowledge 与复杂推理之间的技能冲突，以及 math/coding 数据收益依赖质量阈值，这些观察对大模型数据工程是有信息量的。若实验部分扎实，这类方法比单纯做 proxy regression 更接近长期可用的 mixture optimizer。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是把数据配比优化写成带协变量的连续处理因果推断问题。每次 proxy 训练 run 记为三元组 (X, T, Y)：X 是训练前可观测的数据状态，包含质量、难度、复杂度、风格等统计特征；T 是各域 mixture；Y 是训练后的下游性能。作者强调 X 不能包含任何训练后模型信息或评测结果，否则会破坏因果设定。

处理变量 T 不是直接用 simplex 上的原始比例，而是先做 log-mixture 变换 z=log(t+ε)。这样做有两个原因：一是经验 scaling law 常表现为边际收益递减，log 空间更适合局部线性近似；二是 compositional data 在 simplex 上直接回归不稳定，Aitchison 风格的几何处理更自然。随后作者不去拟合完整响应面 μ(x,z)，而是在历史 mixture 支持域附近采用 partially linear approximation：Y≈g(X)+θ(X)^T z+noise。这里 g(X) 表示由数据状态决定的基线性能，θ(X) 是状态条件化的边际数据回报向量。θ_k(X)>0 表示在当前数据状态下提高第 k 个域占比通常有利，θ_k(X)<0 则意味着可能存在负迁移或技能冲突。

为了从观测到的历史 run 中识别 θ(X)，作者使用 Double Machine Learning 和 causal forest。具体思路是先分别拟合 outcome model 和 treatment model，对 Y 与 T 关于 X 的可预测部分做 orthogonalization / residualization，再在残差空间里估计局部线性效应。这样做的目的是把“数据池本身更好，所以性能更高”与“某个域比例更高，所以性能更高”分开，减少混杂偏差。得到 CATE 估计后，作者不是直接跳到新的最优配比，而是做 trust-region 约束下的保守更新，避免由于局部估计噪声把 mixture 一步推到训练支持域之外。这一点很关键，因为历史 proxy run 只有有限覆盖，过度外推很容易失真。

与 RegMix 一类方法相比，差别不在于用了更复杂的回归器，而在于目标函数变了。RegMix 更像学习一个静态全局 surrogate；CausalMix 学的是“在给定数据状态下，沿哪个方向改 mixture 更可能带来真实收益”。这使它天然更适合数据池变化、模型规模迁移和解释分析。论文还把 CATE 用于分析域间相互作用，而不是只输出一个配比建议，这让方法从纯黑盒调参器变成了可诊断工具。
summary.experiments:
论文的关键实验设置是基于 512 次 Qwen2.5-0.5B proxy runs 拟合因果模型，然后把学到的 mixture 更新策略迁移到未见数据池和更大模型上。仅从当前提供的全文片段，能明确确认的数字主要是这 512 次代理实验和基座规模 0.5B。作者声称方法在底层数据池发生变化时不需要重新做整套 proxy 搜索，能够外推到全新数据池与更大架构，这正是论文最重要的实验主张。

从引言可读出的结果方向有三类。第一，transfer：相较依赖静态分布假设的 proxy mixture 方法，CausalMix 在 unseen data pools 和 larger model architectures 上仍能给出有效配比更新。第二，interpretability：CATE 分析揭示 factual knowledge 与 complex logical reasoning 之间存在技能冲突，说明某些知识型数据增加后可能压制复杂推理收益；同时 math 和 coding 数据并非总是越多越好，其正收益依赖数据质量跨过某个阈值。第三，optimization behavior：作者采用 trust-region 的保守更新，而不是激进重配比，暗示实验里局部边际估计比全局最优搜索更稳定。

不过，当前片段没有给出完整主表，因此还缺少几个决定性细节：具体比较了哪些 baseline；在目标任务上提升了多少绝对点数或相对百分比；迁移到多大模型；数据状态特征具体有哪些、各自贡献多大；以及消融中 DML、causal forest、log-mixture、trust-region 各自的必要性。精读时应重点补这些数字，否则很难判断它是“概念上合理”还是“工程上确实可用”。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇适合精读。先看 Methodology，把三个对象分清：X 是数据状态，T 是 mixture，Y 是训练后性能。只要这三者关系看明白，整篇就通了。接着重点看部分线性近似和 orthogonalization 的推导，理解作者为什么不直接拟合全局 response surface，而是估计局部边际回报 θ(X)。如果你做过 data mixture 或 curriculum，会很容易看出这里的关键不是因果术语本身，而是把“配比规律”和“数据池状态”拆开。

实验部分建议优先看四类内容：1）主结果表，确认在 seen / unseen data pools、不同模型规模上的迁移效果；2）ablation，尤其是去掉数据状态特征、去掉 DML、改成普通回归、去掉 trust-region 后会怎样；3）CATE 可解释性图，看看作者如何支持 skill conflict 和 quality threshold 这两个结论；4）case study，观察方法给出的 mixture 更新方向是否符合直觉，是否会出现过度偏向某一域的失败案例。

如果时间有限，先读 Figure 1、方法总览、主结果表和解释性分析图，大约 45-60 分钟能形成较完整判断。值得深挖的点有三个：数据状态特征是否足够稳定、能否迁移到 pretrain 而不只是 SFT；局部线性假设在更大域数和更稀疏支持下是否仍成立；以及这种因果化 mixture optimizer 能否与 online data selection 或 mid-training annealing 结合。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a practical failure mode in data-mixture optimization for LLM training, especially in SFT: existing methods usually learn a global mapping from mixture weights to downstream performance from historical proxy runs, implicitly assuming that the optimal mixture is stable across data pools. The authors argue that this is false. Once the underlying pool changes in quality, difficulty, style, or complexity, the marginal value of each domain can change substantially, including sign flips from positive transfer to negative transfer. The real problem, then, is not to memorize one best recipe, but to estimate how the return of each domain depends on the current state of the data pool.
summary_en.importance: This is a strong fit for pretraining-adjacent research because it reframes mixture design as a transferable estimation problem rather than a one-off hyperparameter search. The contribution matters in three ways. First, it separates data-state effects from mixture effects, which is exactly the confounding that often makes mixture heuristics brittle in pretraining, continual pretraining, and curriculum design. Second, it aims to learn state-conditioned marginal returns that can transfer to unseen pools and larger models, which is much closer to a scalable recipe-learning setup than static proxy regression. Third, the method produces interpretable conditional treatment effects, and the paper uses them to surface concrete phenomena such as conflicts between factual knowledge and complex reasoning, and quality thresholds for math and code data. That makes it useful not only as an optimizer but also as a diagnostic tool for data engineering.
summary_en.technical_approach:
CausalMix formulates each proxy training run as a triplet (X, T, Y), where X is the pre-training data state, T is the domain mixture, and Y is the downstream performance after training. A key modeling choice is that X contains only pre-training statistics of the data pool, such as quality, difficulty, complexity, entropy, or style, and explicitly excludes any post-training model signal or evaluation outcome.

The treatment is not modeled directly on the simplex. Instead, the paper uses a log-mixture representation z = log(t + epsilon). This choice is motivated by two considerations: empirical diminishing returns are often closer to linear in log space, and compositional data are better handled with geometry-aware transforms than with raw simplex coordinates. Rather than fitting the full response surface mu(x, z), the paper adopts a partially linear local approximation, Y ≈ g(X) + theta(X)^T z + noise. Here g(X) captures the baseline performance implied by the data state, while theta(X) is the state-conditioned marginal return vector. Positive theta_k(X) means increasing domain k is locally beneficial under state X; negative values indicate local negative transfer or domain conflict.

To identify theta(X) from observational proxy runs, the paper uses Double Machine Learning and causal forests. The idea is to first model the predictable parts of both outcome and treatment from X, then residualize them and estimate the local linear effect in the orthogonalized space. This is the crucial step: it tries to disentangle “this pool performs better because the pool itself is better” from “this pool performs better because the mixture changed.” Once the conditional effect is estimated, the method performs a conservative trust-region update rather than jumping directly to an unconstrained optimum. That design is sensible because historical proxy runs only cover a limited region of the mixture space, and aggressive extrapolation would be unreliable.

Compared with methods such as RegMix, the main difference is not just a stronger regressor. The target itself changes. RegMix-style methods learn a static global surrogate from mixture to performance. CausalMix instead estimates a local, state-conditioned causal direction for how to move the mixture under the current pool. That makes it more suitable for distribution shift, transfer across model scales, and interpretation. The paper also uses the estimated CATEs to analyze domain interactions, which is more informative than returning a single recommended mixture.
summary_en.experiments:
The core experimental setup uses 512 proxy runs of Qwen2.5-0.5B to fit the causal model, then tests whether the learned update rule transfers to unseen data pools and larger model architectures. From the provided text, these are the only hard numbers that can be confirmed directly: 512 runs and a 0.5B proxy model. The central empirical claim is that, unlike static-distribution mixture optimizers, CausalMix does not require retraining the proxy search from scratch when the data pool changes.

The reported findings, as described in the paper text, fall into three buckets. First, transfer: the learned causal update generalizes to unseen pools and larger models. Second, interpretability: the estimated conditional treatment effects reveal a conflict between factual-knowledge-heavy data and complex logical reasoning, and show that math and coding data become beneficial only above certain quality thresholds. Third, optimization behavior: trust-region updates appear more stable than aggressive reweighting, which is consistent with the local nature of the estimator.

What still needs to be checked in the full results section are the decisive quantitative details: which baselines were compared, the absolute and relative gains, how large the transfer models are, which data-state features matter most, and how much each component contributes in ablations. In particular, the necessity of DML, causal forests, log-mixture parameterization, and trust-region updates should be verified carefully.
summary_en.reading_guide:
This one is worth a close read. Start with the methodology and keep the three variables straight: X is the data state, T is the mixture, and Y is post-training performance. Once that framing is clear, the rest of the paper becomes much easier to parse. The next thing to focus on is why the paper estimates local marginal returns theta(X) instead of fitting a global response surface. That is the conceptual center of the work. If you have worked on data mixture or curriculum learning, the key insight is not the causal vocabulary by itself, but the explicit separation between pool-state effects and mixture effects.

In the experiments, prioritize four parts: the main transfer results on seen versus unseen pools and across model scales; the ablations removing data-state features, DML, trust-region constraints, or replacing the method with plain regression; the CATE visualizations supporting the skill-conflict and quality-threshold claims; and any case studies showing how the recommended mixture shifts under different pool states. Those sections will tell you whether the method is merely plausible or actually robust.

If time is limited, read Figure 1, the method overview, the main result tables, and the interpretability figures first. The most interesting follow-up questions are whether the chosen data-state features remain stable enough for real deployment, whether the same framework can scale from SFT to pretraining, whether the local linear assumption survives with more domains and sparser support, and whether this causal optimizer can be combined with online data selection or mid-training annealing.

recommendation.zh: 直接解决预训练数据混合的动态泛化痛点，因果建模+小规模实验外推的思路应立刻加入内部数据配比ablation流程
recommendation.en: Directly addresses the dynamic generalization pain point of pretraining data mixture; the causal modeling + small-scale extrapolation workflow should be immediately added to internal data ratio ablation pipelines

paper.title: DataComp-VLM: Improved Open Datasets for Vision-Language Models
paper.abstract: Building performant Vision-Language Models (VLMs) requires carefully curating large-scale training datasets, yet the community lacks systematic benchmarks for evaluating such curation strategies. We introduce DataComp for VLMs (DCVLM), a benchmark for controlled data-centric experiments to improve VLM training. As part of DCVLM, we collect 160 datasets spanning four data types -- image-caption pairs, multimodal interleaved documents, text-only, and instruction-tuning data -- into a corpus of 6T

summary.core_problem: 当前自回归VLM的预训练研究长期聚焦架构和训练流程优化，缺乏标准化的对照基准支撑数据策展研究：公开训练数据规模远低于工业级落地所用的万亿token级别，评估协议不统一，过滤、混合、采样、格式化等常见数据操作的实际效果没有量化结论，主流VLM的数据配方大多不可复现。
summary.importance: 这是继对比学习VLM领域的DataComp、文本LLM领域的DCLM和FineWeb之后，第一个面向现代自回归VLM的开放数据策展基准。它把VLM预训练研究从架构优先的轨道拉回到可控数据实验的方向，给出的结论可以直接指导VLM预训练的混合比例设计，同时公开了6T多模态token数据池、全流程实验框架、多尺度模型checkpoint，是社区开展VLM数据研究的公共基础设施。
summary.technical_approach: 遵循控制变量实验原则，固定模型架构、训练流程、评估管线，仅将数据策展作为独立变量开展实验。首先整合160个公开数据集，构建总规模6T多模态token的统一数据池，覆盖图-文配对、交错多模态文档、纯文本、多模态指令数据四类核心数据类型。设计覆盖1B-8B参数、6.25B-200B训练token的scaling阶梯，适配不同算力预算下的实验需求。评估套件经过稳定性过滤，拆分为验证集、核心集、扩展集三层，覆盖9个领域共52个下游基准。团队完成超过1000组对照实验，量化不同数据策展操作的独立效果。
summary.experiments: 核心实验结论包括三点：第一，在已经经过上游策展的公开数据集上，额外叠加CLIP分数阈值、图像质量过滤等操作的收益极低，甚至带来负效果，和文本LLM从原始CommonCrawl爬取数据开始过滤的场景存在本质差异。第二，数据混合比例是影响性能的核心杠杆，远大于过滤操作的效果；指令数据占比更高的混合配方展现出更好的scaling特性，随着模型参数增大、训练token数增加，重指令配比重图文 caption配比的性能优势持续扩大。第三，预训练阶段的性能排名和SFT后的性能排名皮尔逊相关系数达到0.99，使用Qwen2.5-Base或Qwen2.5-Instruct初始化得到的数据策略排序基本一致，说明预训练阶段得到的数据结论可以稳定迁移到后训练阶段。最终得到的DCVLM-Baseline数据集，在8B参数、200B token训练规模下，核心基准平均得分63.6%，比之前表现最好的公开数据集FineVision高出5.4个百分点。
summary.reading_guide: 重点阅读第4章的核心实验结论，尤其是4.1节过滤与混合操作的效果对比、4.2节不同混合比例的scaling曲线；第3章关注基准设计细节，包括数据池构成、评估集的筛选逻辑。可以重点深挖不同数据类型的scaling law拟合结果，思考为什么额外过滤在预策展数据集上失效，以及多模态数据课程和纯文本数据课程的设计差异。
summary.authors_note: 由LAION、斯坦福大学、华盛顿大学等机构的团队完成，是DataComp、DCLM系列数据基准的延续工作。

summary_en.core_problem: Autoregressive vision-language model (VLM) pretraining research has long prioritized architecture and training recipe improvements, with no standardized controlled benchmark for data curation studies. Public VLM training datasets are orders of magnitude smaller than the trillion-token corpora used for production models, evaluation protocols are inconsistent across publications, the quantitative impact of common curation operations (filtering, mixing, sampling, formatting) remains unmeasured, and most production VLM data recipes are not reproducible.
summary_en.importance: DCVLM is the first open data curation benchmark built for modern autoregressive VLMs, following the controlled experiment paradigm established by DataComp for contrastive VLMs, and DCLM/FineWeb for text LLMs. It shifts VLM pretraining research toward systematic, controlled data experimentation, provides actionable findings that directly inform VLM data mixture design, and releases a 6T multimodal token pool, full experiment infrastructure, and multi-scale checkpoints as shared public infrastructure for the community.
summary_en.technical_approach: The benchmark holds model architecture, training recipe, and evaluation pipeline fixed to isolate data curation as the only experimental variable. The team assembles a unified 6T multimodal token pool from 160 public datasets, spanning four core data types: image-caption pairs, interleaved multimodal documents, text-only corpora, and multimodal instruction tuning data. A structured scaling ladder covering 1B–8B parameter models and 6.25B–200B training token budgets is defined to support experiments across compute regimes. The evaluation suite is filtered for benchmark reliability, split into validation, core, and extended tiers covering 52 downstream tasks across 9 domains. Over 1000 controlled experiments are run to quantify the independent impact of individual curation choices.
summary_en.experiments: Three core findings emerge: First, additional quality filters (e.g., CLIP score thresholds, image quality filters) applied to already curated public datasets deliver minimal to negative returns, a sharp contrast to the large gains seen when filtering raw web crawls for text LLM training. Second, data mixture ratio is the dominant performance lever, with far larger impact than filtering; instruction-heavy mixtures exhibit better scaling properties, and the performance gap between instruction-heavy and caption-heavy mixtures widens as model size and training token budget increase. Third, pretraining performance rankings transfer almost perfectly to post-SFT performance, with a Pearson correlation of r=0.99 across 54 SFT runs, and rankings are robust to LLM initialization choice (Qwen2.5-Base vs Qwen2.5-Instruct), validating the use of pretraining-only metrics for data curation experiments. The final DCVLM-Baseline dataset achieves 63.6% average score on the core benchmark at the 8B/200B token scale, a 5.4 percentage point improvement over the prior best open dataset FineVision.
summary_en.reading_guide: Prioritize Chapter 4 for core experimental results, specifically Section 4.1 comparing effects of filtering vs mixing, and Section 4.2 for scaling curves across mixture ratios. Review Chapter 3 for benchmark design details, including data pool composition and evaluation set filtering criteria. Readers extending the work can dig into scaling law fits across data types, and explore the mechanism behind the limited utility of additional filtering on pre-curated datasets, as well as differences between multimodal and text-only data curriculum design.
summary_en.authors_note: The work is completed by a multi-institution team including LAION, Stanford University, and the University of Washington, as a direct extension of the earlier DataComp and DCLM benchmark series.

recommendation.zh: 这篇会直接影响你做多模态 pretrain 的数据配方：先别迷信过滤器，优先复现 mixture 曲线；摘要之外重点看不同 token budget 下 instruction 比例怎么改斜率。
recommendation.en: This should change your multimodal data recipe prior: stop over-indexing on filtering and reproduce the mixture scaling curves first; the key signal is how instruction-heavy mixes change slope across token budgets.

paper.title: CORTEX: High-Quality Cross-Domain Organization of Web-Scale Corpora through Ontological Corpus Graph
paper.abstract: The continuous evolution of large language models drives escalating demands on data scale and quality, and as different training stages impose increasingly tailored data requirements, systematic organization of high-quality corpora becomes indispensable. Existing corpus construction pipelines confine the resulting corpora to flat, undifferentiated document collections, universally lacking systematic knowledge organization. We present Cortex, to our knowledge the first framework that elevates web

summary.core_problem: 如何把“网页级语料清洗”从扁平的文档过滤，升级为可扩展、可检索、可按训练阶段/领域精细切片的“结构化语料组织”，同时在万亿 token 量级上仍能做多维质量评估而不被教师 LLM 成本压垮。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接价值在两点：第一，把质量评估从单一分数/二分类提升为多维度、可蒸馏的质量信号，并用更贴近标注序关系的损失（OAR）把教师能力压到 0.3B 学生上，解决“高质量打分不可规模化”的老问题；第二，用 Ontological Corpus Graph（内容层-轻量本体层-对齐层）把语料组织成可按本体层级抽取、可做跨域邻接扩展的数据结构，天然适配 continual pretrain / mid-train 的“按域配比与课程”需求。整体贡献更像一套可落地的数据工程+训练接口，而不是单点模型改动。
summary.technical_approach:
Cortex 的核心是三层异构图 OCG。
1) 高质量内容层：从 Common Crawl WARC 到预处理语料 D0，再到 refined 语料。与常见流水线相比，作者强调保留结构化元数据（例如用 Trafilatura 抽取发布时间等），并引入“时间相关性分类器”等组件（全文后续章节应给出细节）。质量评估采用知识蒸馏：用教师 LLM 做多维质量打分，再训练 0.3B 学生在大规模上复现教师的排序/分档能力。关键点是 Ordinal-Aware Regression (OAR) loss：不是把质量当连续回归或硬分类，而是显式利用“等级/序关系”来训练，使学生在边界样本上更稳。
2) 轻量本体层：用 LLM 驱动的自动演化构建层级化概念链集合（Concept Chain Set）。这里的取舍是“轻量”：不追求知识图谱那种高成本实体对齐与关系抽取，而是追求可扩展的层级 taxonomy，服务于语料切片与跨域邻接。
3) 对齐层：把文档/片段与本体概念对齐，并用 Typicality–Fidelity–Specificity (TFS) 加权链接。直觉上：Typicality 约束“像不像该概念域的典型文本”，Fidelity 约束“是否忠实覆盖概念语义”，Specificity 控制“粒度是否足够具体”。通过 TFS 权重，既能做域内抽取，也能沿图做“邻域链”（neighbor-chain）扩展，形成跨域混合数据供 continual pretrain。
此外，作者把 OCG 用作数据合成的结构先验：沿跨域关联生成搜索-推理型 QA，构建 CortexBench，用来反证语料组织与跨域关联的有效性。
summary.experiments:
论文给出的关键量化信息包括：
- 质量评估蒸馏：0.3B 学生模型，宣称相对教师实现 1000× 级别的成本压缩（文中写法为“over 1,000× compression”），目标是支撑万亿 token 规模的质量打分。
- 数据产物：计划开源 24.14B token 的 refined 语料及其 OCG。
- 训练验证：在四个 seed model 上做 continual pre-training，对比使用 OCG 组织的 domain-specific 数据与 neighbor-chain 数据（用于检验“按域切片”和“跨域邻接扩展”是否带来收益）。
- 评测验证：用 OCG 驱动合成 CortexBench（跨域 search-and-reasoning QA），并在 8 个前沿 LLM 上用稳定协议评测，强调题目难度与区分度。
由于你提供的全文片段在方法与引言处截断，具体的性能数字（例如 perplexity/下游指标提升、不同 routing/配比的增益、OAR 相对 MSE/CE 的提升幅度、CortexBench 的分数分布）需要在实验章节表格中补齐；精读时应优先把这些数字抠出来，否则很难判断它是“工程可用”还是“概念好看”。
summary.reading_guide:
建议按“能否复用到自家 pretrain 数据管线”的顺序读：
- 先看 Table 1（与现有 pipeline 的差异点）和 Figure 1（OCG 三层结构与 Stage I–III 的数据流）。
- 精读质量蒸馏部分：教师打分维度定义、标注/采样策略、OAR loss 的形式与为何优于普通回归/分类、学生模型的校准与稳定性（是否跨语言/跨域泛化）。
- 精读对齐层：TFS 三个量的可计算定义、权重如何学习/设定、对“域抽取 vs 邻域扩展”的影响。
- 看 continual pretrain 的实验设计：控制变量是否干净（同 token 数、同训练步数、同 mixture），以及 neighbor-chain 是否只是“更像高质量混合”而非真正的结构收益。
- 最后看 CortexBench 合成：合成模板是否过拟合某类推理、是否引入分布偏置；以及它与 OCG 的对应关系是否可解释。

summary_en.core_problem: How to move web-scale corpus construction beyond flat document filtering into a scalable, structured organization that supports stage-/domain-specific slicing and cross-domain expansion, while keeping multi-dimensional quality assessment feasible at trillion-token scale without relying on expensive teacher LLMs at inference time.
summary_en.importance: The paper matters to pretraining mainly as a data/recipe interface rather than a model tweak. (1) It operationalizes multi-dimensional quality signals via teacher-to-student distillation and an ordinal-aware objective, targeting a practical bottleneck: high-quality scoring does not scale. (2) It introduces an Ontological Corpus Graph (content layer + lightweight ontology + alignment layer) that makes the corpus queryable by taxonomy level and enables graph-based cross-domain neighbor expansion—useful for continual pretraining, mid-training, and curriculum-style mixture control.
summary_en.technical_approach:
CORTEX builds a three-layer heterogeneous structure called OCG.
1) High-Quality Content Layer: a standard CC WARC-to-text pipeline with an emphasis on retaining structured metadata (e.g., publication time) and adding components like temporal relevance filtering. Quality is assessed via distillation: a teacher LLM provides multi-aspect ratings; a 0.3B student is trained to reproduce the teacher’s ordering/grades at scale. The key is the Ordinal-Aware Regression (OAR) loss, treating quality as ordinal rather than pure regression or hard classification.
2) Lightweight Ontology Layer: an LLM-driven, automatically evolving hierarchical “concept chain” taxonomy. The design choice is to keep it lightweight (taxonomy-level organization) instead of building a full knowledge graph with costly entity linking and relation extraction.
3) Alignment Layer: links documents to ontology concepts with Typicality–Fidelity–Specificity (TFS) weighted edges. The intent is to support both domain extraction (fine-grained slicing) and cross-domain association analysis / neighbor-chain expansion.
The graph is also used as a structural prior for data synthesis: cross-domain links guide the generation of search-and-reasoning QA instances, forming CortexBench.
summary_en.experiments:
Key concrete facts stated in the paper excerpt:
- Distilled scorer: 0.3B student, claimed >1000× compression vs teacher LLM cost, intended for trillion-token-scale scoring.
- Data release: a 24.14B-token refined corpus plus its OCG.
- Continual pretraining: conducted on four seed models, comparing OCG-organized domain-specific data and neighbor-chain data.
- Benchmarking: CortexBench is synthesized from OCG and evaluated on eight frontier LLMs under a fixed protocol, positioned as difficult and discriminative.
The provided content is truncated before the main results tables; to judge impact, you need the actual deltas (e.g., gains from OAR vs baselines, pretraining improvements under controlled token budgets, and CortexBench score distributions).
summary_en.reading_guide:
Read it like a reusable corpus pipeline spec:
- Start with Figure 1 (end-to-end stages) and Table 1 (what is genuinely different from prior pipelines).
- Then focus on the distillation section: teacher rating schema, sampling, the exact OAR formulation, calibration, and cross-domain/language robustness.
- Next, inspect the alignment layer: how TFS is computed, how weights are set/learned, and whether it yields interpretable, stable links.
- For the continual pretraining study, verify controls (same tokens/steps/mixtures) and whether neighbor-chain benefits persist beyond “better mixture” effects.
- Finally, check CortexBench synthesis for distribution bias and whether the benchmark truly reflects cross-domain association rather than templated QA generation.

recommendation.zh: 值得看方法和实验设置；若只停在语料图检索，对 pretrain actionability 会打折。
recommendation.en: Read the method and setup; if the gains stop at corpus retrieval, its pretraining actionability is limited.

paper.title: Holistic Data Scheduler for LLM Pre-training via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
paper.abstract: The composition of training data, governed by the diversity of sources and their mixing strategy, is a cornerstone of Large Language Model (LLM) pre-training. Online Data Mixing (ODM), the technique of adaptively adjusting data mixtures during training, has emerged as a promising direction to improve efficiency. However, existing methods are constrained by their reliance on a singular optimization perspective, which fundamentally overlooks the need for complex LLM pre-training to consider the dy

summary.core_problem: 论文研究在线数据配比：预训练过程中如何根据模型状态动态调整不同数据域的采样概率，而不是使用固定 mixture 或只优化单一信号。
summary.importance: 对预训练数据研究的启发在于，它把 data mixture 当作连续控制问题，并把 reward 从单一 loss 或梯度对齐扩展到多信号组合。这个方向值得泛读，但要关注成本和可扩展性。在线调度如果需要频繁计算跨域梯度影响、维护 actor-critic、调 reward 权重，在大规模训练中可能比静态 recipe 或 proxy-based 方法更难落地。
summary.technical_approach: HDS 将预训练过程形式化为 MDP。环境是正在训练的 LLM；状态向量包含当前性能、学习速度和内部稳定性；动作是下一阶段各数据域的采样概率。优化算法使用 Soft Actor-Critic，适合连续动作空间，并通过熵正则鼓励探索。actor 和 critic 使用紧凑的 Transformer-like 网络来编码状态和数据域重要性。核心设计是 multi-objective reward：一部分来自数据质量，一部分来自梯度驱动的 inter-domain influence，延续 AC-ODM 中的 gradient alignment 思路；另一部分来自模型侧信号，例如特定层的 weight norm，用来鼓励收敛和稳定。相较 DoReMi、DoGE、RegMix 这类静态配比方法，HDS 允许配比随训练状态变化；相较 ODM 的 bandit loss reward 和 AC-ODM 的 DDPG gradient alignment，它试图同时使用数据、梯度和模型内部状态。
summary.experiments: 主要结果来自 Pythia-1B 在 The Pile 上的预训练实验。论文报告 HDS 达到先前最佳在线方法的最终 validation perplexity 时，所需 iterations 减少 22%；相比静态 The Pile Weights baseline，iterations 减少 57%。在 MMLU 0-shot 上，HDS 相比先前最佳方法提升 7.2%。这些结果说明多信号在线调度可能改善收敛速度和下游泛化。泛读时需要检查消融：三个 reward 分量各自贡献多少、SAC 相比 DDPG 或 bandit 的收益是否来自算法本身、是否控制了额外计算开销、调度策略是否在不同模型规模和数据域划分下稳定。
summary.reading_guide: 建议用 20 到 30 分钟泛读。优先看 MDP formulation、state/action/reward 的具体定义，以及 Figure 1 的收敛曲线。然后看 reward ablation 和数据域权重随训练变化的图。最后检查训练成本：每次更新 scheduler 是否需要额外 forward/backward，gradient alignment 的计算频率是多少，actor-critic 的训练是否会引入不稳定。若只关心大规模预训练 recipe，重点看方法是否能转化为低频调度或离线蒸馏出的 mixture schedule。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses online data mixing for LLM pretraining: how to adapt domain sampling probabilities during training based on the model’s current state, instead of relying on a fixed mixture or a single optimization signal.
summary_en.importance: The useful idea is to frame data mixture scheduling as a continuous-control problem with multiple feedback signals. This is relevant to pretraining data research because mixture quality often determines convergence speed and capability allocation. The paper is worth skimming rather than reading in full unless the implementation details are needed. The open question is operational cost. A scheduler that depends on gradient influence signals, actor-critic training, and tuned reward weights may be harder to deploy in large-scale training than static recipes or proxy-model approaches.
summary_en.technical_approach: HDS formulates LLM pretraining as an MDP. The environment is the training run. The state vector represents current performance, learning velocity, and internal stability. The action is a probability distribution over data domains for future sampling. The policy is trained with Soft Actor-Critic, which fits the continuous action space and uses entropy regularization for exploration. The actor and critic are compact Transformer-like networks. The main design choice is the reward: it combines a data-quality term, a gradient-driven inter-domain influence term inspired by gradient alignment in AC-ODM, and a model-centric stability term based on layer weight norms. Compared with static approaches such as DoReMi, DoGE, and RegMix, HDS changes the mixture throughout training. Compared with ODM-style bandit rewards or AC-ODM’s narrower gradient-alignment reward, it uses a broader set of signals.
summary_en.experiments: The reported main experiment pretrains Pythia-1B on The Pile. HDS reaches the final validation perplexity of the best reported online baseline with 22% fewer iterations, and with 57% fewer iterations than the static The Pile Weights baseline. On MMLU 0-shot, it reports a 7.2% gain over the best reported baseline. The important checks are the ablations: how much each reward component contributes, whether SAC itself matters compared with DDPG or bandit-style policies, whether the extra scheduler cost is included, and whether the learned schedule remains stable across model sizes and domain partitions.
summary_en.reading_guide: A 20- to 30-minute skim is enough for most pretraining readers. Focus on the MDP definition, especially the exact state features, action parameterization, and reward equations. Then inspect Figure 1 for convergence behavior and look for reward ablations and domain-weight trajectories. The practical question is whether the scheduler can be converted into a low-frequency controller or distilled into an offline mixture schedule. If the method requires frequent extra gradient computations, its usefulness at larger scale will depend on careful systems accounting.

recommendation.zh: 用 SAC 做在线 data mixture 思路新，但奖励设计决定成败；先看 §3 reward 定义和 ablations，再判断能否在内部复现。
recommendation.en: Using SAC for online data mixing is a fresh angle, but the reward design is make-or-break; read §3 and the ablations first before deciding whether to replicate internally.

paper.title: Hubs or Fringes: Pretraining Data Selection via Web Graph Centrality
paper.abstract: The performance of modern language models depends critically on pretraining data composition. Yet existing data selection methods rely on auxiliary classifiers for document scoring or mixture optimization, adding computational overhead and dependence on labeled data. We propose WebGraphMix, a lightweight data selection framework that computes structural centrality scores over the Common Crawl host-level web graph and uses them to vary the proportion of central versus peripheral documents in the

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文解决的是预训练数据选择中过度依赖“单文档内容打分”的问题。现有数据管线通常把网页当作独立样本，用质量分类器、领域分类器或小规模 proxy 训练来决定采样权重。这类方法有两个限制：一是需要额外模型、标注或调参；二是忽略了网页之间的链接结构。WebGraphMix 的问题设定是：Common Crawl 不只是一个文档集合，也是一个大规模 Web 图；网页所在 host 的图位置，可能携带与预训练能力相关的信号。中心节点可能提供更可迁移的通用抽象，边缘节点可能提供更长尾、更专门的知识。
summary.importance: 这项工作的价值不在于给出一个复杂的新模型，而在于把“Web 图拓扑”引入预训练数据配比，并证明它和内容质量信号有互补性。对基座预训练研究来说，这是一类低成本、可复用、无需训练打分器的数据选择信号。它补上了 DCLM、FineWeb、RefinedWeb 等管线中较少显式建模的一块：网页之间的结构关系。贡献量级属于中等偏实用：不是替代质量过滤或领域 mixture optimization，而是提供一个可叠加的维度。尤其值得注意的是，中心数据和边缘数据对不同能力族的影响不同，这说明“高质量数据”不能只被压缩成一个标量分数；结构位置可能对应不同的能力增益。
summary.technical_approach: WebGraphMix 使用 Common Crawl 的 host-level hyperlink graph。图中每个节点是一个 host，例如 wikipedia.org；有向边表示 host 之间的超链接。论文使用的图规模为 13.9M 个节点、439.6M 条边。方法不是对每篇文档训练一个质量模型，而是先在 host 图上计算中心性分数，再把该 host 下的文档映射到对应分数，并据此构造预训练采样混合。主要测试两类中心性：Betweenness centrality 和 Katz centrality。Betweenness 衡量一个节点出现在大量最短路径上的程度，更像“桥接不同社区”的信号；Katz centrality 衡量一个节点与高影响节点的连接程度，带有传播式影响力的含义。论文也尝试了 PageRank，但没有观察到提升，这和 DCLM 中 PageRank 类信号效果有限的观察一致。实验设计上，作者构造偏中心、偏边缘、中心/边缘混合等数据子集，并固定 tokenizer、shuffle、优化器和训练流程，以尽量隔离数据选择本身的影响。进一步地，论文把中心性分数与 DCLM-fasttext 质量分类器结合，使用乘法和除法式打分来测试结构信号是否与内容质量信号互补。
summary.experiments: 实验接入标准化的 DataComp-LM pipeline。模型规模包括 400M 和 1B；训练 token 分别为 8B 和 28B。评测使用 DCLM CORE v2 的 23 个任务。中心性计算在完整 Common Crawl host 图上完成，总计算成本少于 9 个 GPU 小时，之后可以复用于不同训练实验。关键结果集中在 1B 规模：只采样结构中心 host 的文档，相比 uniform sampling，在 Symbolic & Algorithmic Reasoning 上提升约 +1.4%；采样结构边缘 host 的文档，则更有利于 Science & Factual Knowledge 以及 Commonsense & Reasoning。这个分化很重要，说明中心和边缘不是简单的优劣关系，而是携带不同类型的学习信号。最有效的基础混合是基于 betweenness 的 50% central + 50% peripheral，23 项平均分达到 41.4%，uniform sampling 为 39.8%。当中心性信号与 DCLM-fasttext 质量分类器组合后，平均分进一步达到 43.8%。这表明 Web 图结构不是质量分类器的重复版本，而是能补充内容打分无法直接看到的信息。
summary.reading_guide: 建议精读方法部分中 host-level graph 的构造、中心性定义、文档到 host 分数的映射方式，以及采样 mixture 的具体实现。实验部分应重点看三类对比：central-only、peripheral-only、central/peripheral mixture；betweenness、Katz、PageRank 的差异；中心性分数与 DCLM-fasttext 质量分数结合后的结果。最值得深挖的是能力分组结果，而不只是 23 项平均分。中心 host 对符号和算法类任务更有帮助，边缘 host 对事实和常识类任务更有帮助，这一现象可能对数据课程、能力定向 mixture、long-tail data reweighting 都有启发。还应关注计算成本和可迁移性：中心性计算只需一次，成本远低于训练 proxy LM 或标注质量分类器。局限也需要一起读：host-level 聚合会丢失同一域名内部的页面差异；中心性分数可能受 SEO、站点模板、链接农场影响；28B token 训练规模仍偏小，结论需要在更大 token budget 和更强模型上验证。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies pretraining data selection beyond independent document scoring. Most current pipelines score or sample web documents using content-based quality classifiers, domain labels, or proxy training. These methods add cost and often ignore the hyperlink structure of the web. WebGraphMix asks whether a document’s position in the host-level web graph contains useful signal for LM pretraining. Central hosts may expose reusable abstractions and bridge heterogeneous topics, while peripheral hosts may carry specialized or long-tail knowledge.
summary_en.importance: The main contribution is a cheap and reusable structural signal for pretraining data curation. It does not replace quality filtering or domain mixture optimization, but adds a different axis: topology of the web graph. This is useful for pretraining research because large web corpora are not just bags of documents; their link structure encodes citation, topic, and authority patterns that standard document classifiers do not directly model. The empirical result that central and peripheral data help different capability groups is also important. It suggests that data quality should not always be reduced to a single scalar score, especially when the goal is to shape model capabilities rather than only improve average validation loss.
summary_en.technical_approach: WebGraphMix operates on the Common Crawl host-level hyperlink graph. Each node is a host, and each directed edge is a hyperlink between hosts. The graph used in the paper has 13.9M nodes and 439.6M edges. The method computes centrality scores on this graph, maps each document to the score of its host, and then constructs pretraining mixtures that emphasize central hosts, peripheral hosts, or a controlled combination of both. The main centrality measures are betweenness centrality and Katz centrality. Betweenness captures bridge-like nodes that lie on many shortest paths, while Katz centrality captures influence propagated through links to other influential nodes. The authors also test PageRank, but it does not improve results, matching a similar observation in DCLM. The experiments are integrated into the DataComp-LM pipeline, with tokenization, shuffling, and optimization held fixed to isolate the effect of data selection. The paper also combines graph centrality with the DCLM-fasttext quality classifier using multiplicative and divisive scoring, testing whether topology adds information beyond content-based quality.
summary_en.experiments: The paper trains 400M and 1B parameter models on 8B and 28B tokens, respectively, and evaluates on 23 tasks from DCLM CORE v2. Computing centrality on the full Common Crawl host graph takes less than 9 GPU hours in total, and the scores can be reused across experiments. At the 1B scale, selecting structurally central hosts improves Symbolic & Algorithmic Reasoning by about +1.4% over uniform sampling. Selecting peripheral hosts improves Science & Factual Knowledge and Commonsense & Reasoning. A 50/50 mixture of central and peripheral data based on betweenness reaches 41.4% average accuracy across the 23 tasks, compared with 39.8% for uniform sampling. Combining graph centrality with the DCLM-fasttext quality classifier further improves the average to 43.8%. The most useful empirical message is not just the average gain, but the capability split: central and peripheral web regions appear to provide different training signals.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read the method section carefully for the host graph construction, the definition of centrality scores, the mapping from hosts to documents, and the sampling procedure. In the experiments, focus on three comparisons: central-only versus peripheral-only sampling, betweenness versus Katz versus PageRank, and graph centrality alone versus graph centrality combined with the DCLM-fasttext quality classifier. The capability-group breakdown is more informative than the overall average because it shows how structural data choices affect different skills. The most interesting follow-up questions are whether the same pattern holds at larger token budgets, whether host-level aggregation hides important page-level variation, and how robust the signal is to spam, SEO artifacts, and link farms. For a pretraining practitioner, the practical appeal is clear: the signal is unsupervised, cheap to compute once, and easy to combine with existing quality filters.

recommendation.zh: 这篇值得认真看：它把“数据质量”从文本表面特征转到网页图结构，若实验干净，会直接影响你做 data mixture 的先验；先看 mixture sweep 和对 classifier baseline 的对照。
recommendation.en: Worth real attention: it shifts data selection from text-local quality signals to web-graph structure; if the controls are clean, it should update your prior on corpus mixture design—read the mixture sweep and classifier-baseline comparisons first.

authors: Vedant Badoni   Danqi Chen   Xinyi Wang{vedantbadoni, danqic}@princeton.eduwangxinyilinda@gmail.comPrinceton Language and Intelligence

paper.title: Towards Engineering Scaling Laws with Pretraining Data Composition
paper.abstract: Neural scaling laws describe how model performance improves as a power law in compute, model size, and dataset size. While well-established for large language models, these relationships are emerging for large models in particle physics. As with language, empirical studies show that the performance scales as a power law. However, unlike natural language or image domains, fundamental physics has high-fidelity simulators that produce synthetic data cheaply. This favors scaling regimes where additi

summary.core_problem: 论文研究的是在高能物理模拟数据场景下，能否通过设计预训练数据组成来改变 scaling law 的形状和 compute-optimal 方向。具体任务是 hadronic jet 分类：固定下游任务，改变 JetClass-II 预训练子集里的物理过程组成，观察模型大小、预训练数据组成和微调性能之间的幂律关系。
summary.importance: 这不是 LLM 论文，领域任务也较窄；对基座预训练的价值在于数据组成与 scaling behavior 的关系。它把“数据更多”拆成更具体的问题：预训练数据是否覆盖更宽的生成过程，是否与下游任务的有效特征对齐。这个视角可以类比到语言模型的数据配比：不同语料不只是改变平均质量，也可能改变 scaling exponent、数据受限还是参数受限的最优区间，以及微调阶段对参数量和数据量的依赖。需要注意，论文中的数据来自可控物理模拟，和自然语言网页语料的采样约束不同，结论不能直接迁移。
summary.technical_approach: 方法使用一个处理 jet point cloud 的通用 Transformer。每个 jet 由 constituent particles 构成，每个粒子包含 4 个运动学特征、4 个轨迹位移特征和 1 个粒子 ID 特征。模型使用 learnable class token、pre-norm Transformer blocks、SwiGLU FFN，不使用位置编码，因为输入是集合而不是序列。模型深度固定为 4 层，attention head dimension 固定为 8，通过改变 embedding dimension 和 head 数得到 12 个模型规模，参数量约从 3K 到 10.5M。预训练数据来自 JetClass-II，共 188 类模拟 jet，分为 QCD、BSM two-prong resonance decay、BSM three/four-prong resonance decay 三组。论文构造四个预训练子集：QCD only、QCD+res2p、QCD+res34p、QCD+res2p+res34p。下游任务是在 JetClass 上做 10 类 jet 分类。核心设计是用 BSM resonance decay 增加预训练数据的 diversity 和 alignment：它们覆盖 QCD 不覆盖的相空间，并在 prong multiplicity、mass scale、substructure 等特征上更接近下游任务。
summary.experiments: 实验扫描 12 个模型规模和多种预训练数据组成，在 JetClass-II 上预训练后，在 JetClass 10 类分类任务上微调，并拟合性能随模型规模和数据组成变化的 scaling behavior。给定正文明确给出了模型规模范围、数据桶和预训练子集设计，但没有提供结果表格里的具体数值、拟合指数或误差下降幅度。可归纳的实验结论是：加入 BSM resonance decay 的预训练子集通过增加多样性和任务相关性，能够改变 fine-tuning scaling 的趋势，使 compute-optimal 分配更偏向使用数据，而不是单纯扩大模型。论文也承认当前实验没有分离 diversity 和 alignment 两个因素，因为 BSM-augmented 数据同时带来更宽支持集和更强下游相关性。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议 15–25 分钟。LLM 研究者不需要细读物理背景，重点看 Introduction 里关于 engineering scaling laws 的问题设定，以及 Methods 里四个预训练子集如何定义 diversity 和 alignment。实验部分优先看 scaling fits、不同数据组成的性能曲线、compute-optimal 讨论。如果关心数据配比研究，可以重点关注作者如何把“数据组成”转化为可控变量；如果只关心通用 LLM 预训练，这篇可以作为方法类旁证，不需要深读物理任务细节。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper asks whether scaling behavior can be engineered by changing the composition of pretraining data. The study is set in hadronic jet classification, where high-fidelity simulators make it cheap to generate controlled pretraining corpora. The concrete question is how different JetClass-II pretraining mixtures affect the scaling relation between model size, data composition, and downstream fine-tuning performance on JetClass.
summary_en.importance: This is a physics-domain study rather than an LLM pretraining paper, so its direct relevance is limited. The useful idea is that data composition can change not only the intercept of a scaling curve but also the regime in which more data or more parameters are preferred. For LLM pretraining, the analogue would be mixtures whose diversity and task alignment affect scaling exponents, downstream transfer, and compute-optimal allocation. The caveat is important: particle physics has controllable synthetic data generation, while language pretraining usually depends on messy, naturally occurring corpora.
summary_en.technical_approach: The model is a Transformer over jet point clouds. Each jet is represented as a set of constituent particles, with kinematic features, trajectory displacement features, and particle identification features. The architecture uses a learnable class token, pre-norm Transformer blocks, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and no positional encodings because the input is a set. Depth is fixed at four layers and the attention head dimension is fixed at eight; embedding width and number of heads are varied to obtain 12 model sizes from roughly 3K to 10.5M parameters. Pretraining uses JetClass-II, which contains 188 simulated jet classes grouped into QCD, two-prong BSM resonance decays, and three/four-prong BSM resonance decays. Four pretraining subsets are compared: QCD only, QCD plus res2p, QCD plus res34p, and the union of all three groups. The downstream task is 10-class jet classification on JetClass. The main design choice is to use BSM resonance decays as a controlled way to increase both distributional diversity and alignment with downstream substructure features.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments sweep model size and pretraining composition, then fine-tune on the JetClass classification task and analyze scaling trends. The available text gives the parameter range, architecture, data buckets, and mixture definitions, but not the exact fitted exponents or numerical performance gains. The reported qualitative result is that BSM-augmented pretraining mixtures alter the scaling behavior and move the preferred allocation toward data-rich regimes. The study also notes a limitation: diversity and alignment are not disentangled, because the BSM additions simultaneously broaden the pretraining support and improve feature overlap with the downstream task.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in 15–25 minutes. For LLM pretraining readers, the useful parts are the introduction’s framing of engineered scaling laws and the methods section defining the four controlled data mixtures. In the results, focus on the scaling fits, mixture comparisons, and compute-allocation discussion. The particle-physics details can be read lightly unless you need to evaluate whether the claimed diversity and alignment variables are well controlled.

recommendation.zh: 数据组成可改变scaling幂律斜率的结论对LLM数据配比设计有直接参考，重点看数据组成调控scaling的实验部分。
recommendation.en: The finding that data composition shifts scaling law exponents is directly relevant to LLM data mixture design; focus on the data-modulated scaling experiments.

paper.title: RegMix-D: Dynamic Data Mixing via Proxy Training Trajectories
paper.abstract: Data mixture selection is critical for Large Language Model pretraining. Existing methods such as RegMix select a single static mixture by fitting a regression model on small-scale proxy runs. We propose RegMix-D, a simple extension of RegMix to dynamic mixing. Our key observation is that proxy runs produce not only endpoint losses, but also full loss trajectories, which can be used to further improve data mixture. By training regression model on these trajectories, we can predict optimal mixtur

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文解决的是预训练数据配比里的一个老问题：不同语料域的最优 mixture 并不是整个训练过程都不变，但现有像 RegMix 这样的做法只用 proxy run 的终点 loss 去选一个静态配比，等于默认“全程一个最优解”。作者要做的是在不引入复杂额外训练机制的前提下，把 proxy 训练轨迹里的时序信息利用起来，得到随训练阶段变化的动态 data mixture schedule。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的意义比较直接，而且量级不小。数据混合比例本来就是 pretrain recipe 里影响很大的自由度，但过去自动化方法大多停留在 static mixture。RegMix-D 的贡献在于证明：只要把 proxy run 从“一个终点样本”改成“多段轨迹样本”，就能在几乎不改变 RegMix 框架的情况下，把静态 mixture 搜索扩展成动态调度，而且还能降低 proxy compute 需求。它不是提出新的优化目标，也不是靠额外 teacher/reference model 做复杂控制，而是把已有 proxy 预算里的信息榨得更干净。这对大规模预训练很有现实意义，因为它同时碰到了两个核心点：data curriculum 和 proxy-based recipe search。
summary.technical_approach:
方法很简洁，关键是把回归目标从“mixture -> 最终 loss”改成“当前训练状态 -> 下一阶段 loss”。RegMix 原始做法是：采样若干 mixture，训练若干小 proxy 模型到固定步数，只记录终点验证损失，再拟合一个回归器预测某个 mixture 的终点 loss，最后选一个全程固定的 mixture。RegMix-D 则在 proxy 训练中按多个时间点记录 validation loss，把每条 proxy trajectory 切成若干相邻区间。对于给定的 switch point 数 N，会选出 N+1 个时间节点 t1...tN+1，并从每条轨迹构造 M×N 个训练样本。回归器 f_N 的输入是当前步点 t_l、当前 mixture m、当前 observed loss l_l，输出是下一时间点的 loss l_{l+1}。也就是说，它学的是局部转移，而不是全局终点映射。

在部署上有两个版本。Offline 版本在目标训练开始前递归生成完整 schedule：从初始 loss 出发，在每个 switch point 上搜索使预测下一段 loss 最低的 mixture，把预测出的 loss 再喂给下一段，直到生成整条 mixture schedule。这个版本不需要 target run 中途干预，但误差会递归累积。Online 版本则在 target training 的每个 switch point 上，用目标模型真实观测到的 validation loss 替代预测 loss，再调用同一个冻结回归器选择下一段 mixture。这样做的好处是把 proxy-to-target 的偏差限制在单段决策里，而不是沿整条 schedule 传播。

方法上的几个细节值得注意。第一，作者没有引入额外 RL、bandit 或 bilevel optimization 机制，仍然是回归 + candidate search，所以工程接入成本低。第二，初始阶段固定使用 human-curated Pile prior，而不是从第一个 segment 就让回归器自由选 mixture，这反映了一个现实假设：训练初期没有足够 target-state 信息，先验配比更稳。第三，mixture 搜索仍然通过 Dirichlet-sampled candidates 完成，说明作者追求的是在现有 RegMix 搜索框架内最小改动地升级为 dynamic mixing，而不是重新设计连续优化器。
summary.experiments:
实验设置沿用 RegMix 标准配置：在 Pile 上做 25B tokens 训练，目标模型为 1B 参数。论文的核心比较对象是静态 RegMix 与动态 RegMix-D，在不同 switch granularity 下比较 offline 和 online 两种部署。主结论有三条。第一，RegMix-D 在所有测试粒度上都优于 RegMix，既体现在 validation loss，也体现在 13 个下游任务的平均表现。第二，online 版本通常比 offline 更稳，因为它用真实 target loss 校正状态，避免递归预测误差累积；offline 仍然有效，但更依赖回归器外推质量。第三，数据效率明显提升：只用 128 个 proxy models，也就是 RegMix 512 个 proxy 配置约 25% 的预算，就已经能超过后者。这一点很关键，因为 proxy-based mixture search 真正的瓶颈往往不是方法本身，而是前期试验成本。

从摘要和正文可见信息看，作者强调的是“一致优于”而不是某个单点大幅提升。更值得注意的是消融逻辑：性能提升来自轨迹监督带来的更好状态建模，而不是单纯因为用了更多 proxy 标签；因为同一条 proxy run 的中间 loss 被重复利用，单位 proxy compute 产出的监督信号更多。另一个重要观察是，动态 mixture 的收益在训练不同阶段并不均匀，这间接支持了作者的出发点：域最优配比确实会随训练进展变化，静态 mixture 只能做折中。
summary.reading_guide: 这篇建议精读。先看 Introduction 和 Figure 1，把问题框成“static mixture selection 不够，因为最优域配比会漂移”。然后重点读 RegMix-D 方法部分，尤其是训练样本构造、f_N 的输入输出定义、offline 递归生成 schedule 的过程，以及 online 如何用真实 loss 做状态校正。这里真正的创新不在模型形式，而在问题重写：把 mixture search 从一次性全局选择改成局部状态转移预测。实验部分优先看三类结果：一是 validation loss 曲线，确认动态调度是否稳定优于静态；二是 13 个下游任务总表，判断收益是否泛化；三是 proxy 数量消融，理解它为什么能用更少 proxy 超过 RegMix。若时间有限，先抓住 offline vs online 的差别，再看不同 switch point 数 N 的敏感性。值得深挖的点有四个：其一，回归器是否真正学到了“阶段性域需求”，还是只是在拟合 loss 平滑趋势；其二，switch granularity 过细时是否会引入 schedule 抖动；其三，proxy-to-target 缩放在更大模型、更长训练上是否仍成立；其四，初始使用 human prior 的设计是否可以被更系统的 cold-start 策略替代。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a central weakness in proxy-based data-mixture optimization for LLM pretraining: the best domain mixture is unlikely to stay constant throughout training, yet methods such as RegMix assume a single static optimum and fit regressors only on endpoint losses from proxy runs. RegMix-D turns the problem into dynamic mixture scheduling by exploiting the full loss trajectories already produced by those proxy runs.
summary_en.importance: This is directly relevant to pretraining practice. Data mixture is one of the highest-leverage recipe choices, but most automated methods still search for one fixed mixture. RegMix-D shows that a dynamic schedule can be obtained with minimal changes to the existing RegMix pipeline, simply by using trajectory supervision instead of endpoint-only supervision. The practical significance is twofold: it improves target-model performance and reduces the amount of proxy compute needed to beat the static baseline. That makes it a meaningful contribution to data curriculum design and proxy-based recipe search.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The key move is to replace a global regression target with a local transition model. In standard RegMix, each sampled mixture is used to train one proxy model to a fixed horizon, only the final validation loss is kept, and a regressor maps mixture to endpoint loss. The chosen mixture is then used for the entire target run. RegMix-D logs validation loss at multiple points along each proxy trajectory. For a chosen number of switch points N, it selects N+1 time anchors and converts each proxy trajectory into M×N training examples. The regressor f_N takes the current state (training step t_l, current mixture m, current loss l_l) and predicts the next loss l_{l+1}. In other words, it learns one-step loss transitions rather than a direct mixture-to-final-loss map.

This enables two deployment modes. In the offline mode, the schedule is generated before target training: starting from an initial loss, the method searches over candidate mixtures at each switch point, picks the one with the lowest predicted next-step loss, feeds that predicted loss into the next decision, and recursively builds a full schedule. In the online mode, the same frozen regressor is queried during target training, but the current loss is the actually observed target-model validation loss rather than the previously predicted one. This grounds each decision in the real target trajectory and limits error accumulation.

Several design choices are worth noting. The method does not introduce RL, bandits, or bilevel optimization; it stays within the regression-plus-search framework, which keeps the engineering overhead low. The first segment uses the human-curated Pile prior instead of a learned mixture, reflecting a cold-start assumption that early in training there is not enough target-state information to trust dynamic adaptation. Candidate mixtures are still searched via Dirichlet sampling, so the contribution is a minimal but effective extension of RegMix rather than a full redesign of the optimizer.
summary_en.experiments:
The experiments follow the standard RegMix setup: a 1B-parameter target model trained on 25B tokens from the Pile. The main comparisons are static RegMix versus RegMix-D, with both offline and online variants evaluated under different switching granularities. The headline findings are consistent. First, RegMix-D outperforms RegMix at every tested granularity, both in validation loss and across 13 downstream tasks. Second, the online variant is generally more reliable than the offline one because it uses observed target losses to correct the state, whereas the offline schedule can accumulate recursive prediction error. Third, the method is notably more proxy-efficient: 128 proxy models, about 25% of the 512-proxy budget used by RegMix, are already enough to surpass the static baseline.

The important experimental point is not one unusually large gain, but the consistency of the improvement. The ablation logic also matters: the benefit comes from extracting more supervision from the same proxy runs, not from adding a new expensive optimization loop. By reusing intermediate losses, each proxy run yields many local transition labels. Another useful observation is that the gains from dynamic mixing are not uniform across training, which supports the paper’s premise that the preferred domain composition shifts over time and cannot be captured well by a single static mixture.
summary_en.reading_guide: This one deserves a close read. Start with the introduction and Figure 1 to frame the problem correctly: static mixture selection is limited because the optimal domain composition drifts during training. Then focus on the RegMix-D section, especially how trajectory samples are constructed, what f_N predicts, how the offline recursive schedule is generated, and how the online variant replaces predicted losses with observed target losses. The main innovation is not a sophisticated model class; it is the reformulation of mixture search as local state-transition prediction. In the experiments, prioritize three pieces: validation-loss comparisons, the 13-task downstream table, and the proxy-budget ablation. If time is limited, first understand the offline-versus-online trade-off, then look at sensitivity to the number of switch points N. The deeper questions are whether the regressor is truly learning stage-dependent domain demand rather than just smoothing loss trends, whether very fine switching causes schedule instability, whether proxy-to-target transfer still holds at larger scales, and whether the human-prior cold start can be replaced by a more principled initialization strategy.

recommendation.zh: 应在内部 data-mixture ablation 里复现；重点看 trajectory 信号是否真能跨尺度迁移。
recommendation.en: Worth reproducing in internal data-mixture ablations; the key question is whether trajectory signals transfer cleanly across scale.

paper.title: FastMix: Fast Data Mixture Optimization via Gradient Descent
paper.abstract: While large and diverse datasets have driven recent advances in large models, identifying the optimal data mixture for pre-training and post-training remains a significant open problem. We address this challenge with FASTMIX, a novel framework that automates data mixture discovery while training only a single proxy model. Instead of relying on predefined heuristics or resource-intensive simulations, FASTMIX jointly optimizes mixture coefficients and model parameters, substantially improving effi

summary.core_problem: 预训练与后训练的数据 mixture 配比通常依赖启发式或多次重训搜索，成本极高，需要在单次代理模型训练内高效优化。
summary.importance: 把 data mixture 搜索明确写成双层优化，并推导出'按源均匀采样等价于按 mixture 系数做 per-source loss 重加权'的等价性，把 mixture 搜索变成端到端可微问题；是 data mixture 自动化方向的重要进展。
summary.technical_approach: FastMix 将 mixture 选择表述为 bilevel optimization；推导得到优化 mixture ratio 等价于在 uniform source sampling 下对每个 source 的 loss 赋权，从而可以在训练一个 proxy model 的过程中，用梯度同时更新模型参数和 mixture 系数，避免了多模型多次重跑。
summary.experiments: 摘要未给出完整实验细节与具体模型/数据规模，但宣称显著优于依赖预定义启发式和多仿真的已有 mixture 搜索方法，在效率与可扩展性上提升明显。

summary_en.core_problem: Finding the optimal data mixture for pre-training and post-training is usually done by heuristics or costly repeated training runs.
summary_en.importance: Reformulates data mixture search as a bilevel optimization problem and shows an equivalence between optimizing mixture ratios and assigning per-source loss weights under uniform source sampling, turning mixture search into an end-to-end differentiable problem.
summary_en.technical_approach: FastMix jointly optimizes mixture coefficients and model parameters in a single proxy run: mixture ratios are embedded into a differentiable training objective via the derived reweighting equivalence, enabling gradient-based mixture updates without repeated full runs.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract claims substantial efficiency and scalability gains over heuristic-based and simulation-heavy prior mixture optimization methods; full model and dataset details are not provided in the abstract.

recommendation.zh: 把 mixture search 从黑盒扫参变成可微双层优化，直接对应 data ratio 调参的真实痛点；应在内部小规模 proxy 上复现这个 reweighting 等价关系。
recommendation.en: Turns data-mixture search from black-box sweeps into differentiable bilevel optimization; worth reproducing the reweighting equivalence on an internal proxy setup.

paper.title: The Culture Funnel: You Can't Align What isn't in the Data
paper.abstract: Current cultural alignment approaches focus on inference-time interventions, assuming models already contain sufficient cultural knowledge. We argue modern LLM pipelines suffer from a cultural data funnel. Using a multidimensional tagging framework across pretraining, fine-tuning, alignment, and reasoning datasets, we show explicit cultural signals decline sharply during post-training, while geographically concentrated, task-specialized data dominates. Multilinguality enhances geographic diversi

summary.core_problem: 这项工作研究文化对齐失败是否来自训练数据管线，而不是只来自推理时提示或对齐方法。核心观点是：预训练语料中可能存在一定文化信号，但经过 SFT、偏好对齐、推理数据和任务化数据筛选后，显式文化信息会被压缩，形成所谓 culture funnel。
summary.importance: 对预训练数据研究的启发比较明确。它把文化对齐从“模型有没有文化知识”转成“训练阶段是否给了模型足够、均衡、可学习的文化信号”。这对 data mixture、post-training 数据配比、合成推理数据污染都有意义。现在很多后训练数据强调数学、代码、推理和通用帮助性，容易把地域、生活方式、社会规范、价值偏好等信号稀释掉。多语数据可以增加地域覆盖，但不能自动保证文化覆盖均衡，这一点对 multilingual pretraining 和 instruction tuning 都有参考价值。
summary.technical_approach: 工作构建了一个自动文化标注管线，对 5.6M 条样本做多维标签。标签维度包括文化类型、领域、任务意图、地理位置和语言。文化标签采用面向 NLP 的 taxonomy，包含 Culture as Knowledge、Dynamics、Preference、Bias，并额外区分 General Culture 和 No Culture。语言识别使用 FastText LangID，其余标注主要使用 Command-A。预训练语料按整段文本标注；后训练和对话数据只标注用户侧 prompt 或 instruction，因为这些部分决定了模型是否有机会学习文化语境。数据选择覆盖预训练、后训练、评测和真实用户对话，包括 CulturaX、Dolci Instruct-SFT、GeoFact-X、CultureBank、MultiNRC、Aya 原创标注、PRISM 和 ShareLM 等。
summary.experiments: 实验结果显示，显式文化信号在训练管线后段明显下降，后训练数据更集中在少数地理区域和任务类型上。多语言数据提升了地理多样性，但语言不是文化的充分代理，仍会出现覆盖不均。工作还报告了一个实用结果：加入显式文化标签后，下游文化 benchmark 表现提升，说明文化标记不只是分析工具，也可以作为训练或数据筛选信号。需要注意的是，标注依赖自动模型，结论更适合作为大规模数据分布诊断，而不是对单条样本文化充分性的人工判定。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议 25 到 35 分钟。先看数据选择和 tagging taxonomy，确认它如何定义文化、地理位置、任务意图和语言。然后看各训练阶段的文化信号变化图表，这是主要结论来源。最后看文化标签用于下游 benchmark 的实验，判断这些标签是否能转化为训练收益。对做数据配比的人，重点不是具体 benchmark 分数，而是它提供了一种审计 post-training 数据的方式：检查指令数据、偏好数据和推理数据是否系统性稀释了文化语境。

summary_en.core_problem: The work asks whether failures in cultural alignment are caused by the training data pipeline rather than only by inference-time prompting or alignment methods. Its central claim is that cultural signals may exist in pretraining corpora, but are progressively compressed during SFT, alignment, reasoning-data construction, and task-specialized post-training.
summary_en.importance: The paper is most relevant as a pretraining and post-training data study. It reframes cultural alignment as a data-mixture and signal-preservation problem: models cannot reliably learn culturally situated behavior if the relevant contexts are sparse, geographically concentrated, or removed by later curation stages. This matters for multilingual pretraining, instruction tuning, synthetic reasoning data, and preference-data design. A useful point is that multilinguality improves geographic coverage but does not by itself provide balanced cultural representation.
summary_en.technical_approach: The authors build an automatic tagging pipeline and apply it to 5.6M samples across datasets from different stages of the LLM pipeline. Each sample is annotated along multiple dimensions: cultural content, domain, task intent, geolocation, and language. The cultural taxonomy includes Culture as Knowledge, Dynamics, Preference, and Bias, with additional labels for General Culture and No Culture. Language is tagged with FastText LangID, while the other annotations are produced mainly with Command-A. For pretraining corpora, the full text is tagged. For post-training and conversational data, only user-side prompts or instructions are tagged, because these determine whether the model is exposed to a culturally grounded learning opportunity. The dataset pool includes CulturaX, Dolci Instruct-SFT, GeoFact-X, CultureBank, MultiNRC, Aya original annotations, PRISM, and ShareLM.
summary_en.experiments: The main empirical finding is a sharp decline of explicit cultural signals in later training stages. Post-training datasets become more geographically concentrated and more dominated by task-specialized content such as reasoning, coding, and generic instruction following. Multilingual data increases geographic diversity but still leaves cultural representation imbalanced. The paper also reports that explicit cultural tags improve performance on downstream cultural benchmarks, suggesting that the tags can be used not only for auditing but also for data selection or training interventions. The main limitation is that the analysis relies on automatic tagging, so the results are best interpreted as large-scale distributional diagnostics rather than fine-grained human judgments of cultural adequacy.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim time: 25–35 minutes. Read the dataset selection and tagging taxonomy first, because the conclusions depend heavily on how culture, geolocation, task intent, and language are operationalized. Then focus on the stage-wise distribution results that show how cultural signals change from pretraining to post-training. The downstream benchmark section is useful for checking whether the tags have training utility. For data researchers, the main value is the audit protocol: inspect whether instruction, preference, and reasoning datasets systematically remove culturally grounded contexts.

recommendation.zh: 读标注体系和各训练阶段的漏斗统计；动作是审数据配比，不是再加推理时补丁。
recommendation.en: Read the taxonomy and stage-wise funnel statistics; the action item is auditing data mixtures, not adding another inference-time patch.

paper.title: Hubs or Fringes: Pretraining Data Selection via Web Graph Centrality
paper.abstract: The performance of modern language models depends critically on pretraining data composition. Yet existing data selection methods rely on auxiliary classifiers for document scoring or mixture optimization, adding computational overhead and dependence on labeled data. We propose WebGraphMix, a lightweight data selection framework that computes structural centrality scores over the Common Crawl host-level web graph and uses them to vary the proportion of central versus peripheral documents in the

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决的是预训练数据选择里一个很具体但长期被忽略的问题：现有方法大多把文档当独立样本，用内容分类器、质量打分器或 mixture optimization 来决定采样比例，却几乎不利用网页之间的链接结构。作者提出的问题不是“哪些网页写得更像高质量文本”，而是“网页在整个 web graph 里的结构位置，是否对应不同类型的可迁移知识，从而影响模型学到的能力”。更进一步，他们想要一个不依赖标注、不训练额外打分模型、能在 web 规模上运行的数据选择方法。
summary.importance:
这篇对预训练研究是实打实有分量的。贡献不在于提出更复杂的筛选器，而在于把数据选择的观察单位从独立文档扩展到图结构中的 host 位置，并且给出可复现的、低成本的 web-scale 实证。它的重要性有三层。

第一，它提供了一个与内容质量信号近似正交的新轴。论文里 centrality 与 DCLM-fasttext 质量分类器结合后还能继续提升，说明图结构不是在重复已有质量分数，而是在补充另一类信息。

第二，它把“数据 mixture 决定能力分布”这件事讲得更细。中心 host 更偏向可复用抽象和桥接性知识，边缘 host 更偏向长尾和专门知识；不同采样会把模型推向不同能力侧重。这比简单说‘高质量数据更好’要具体得多。

第三，它的工程门槛低。13.9M 节点、4.396 亿边的 host graph，全部 centrality 计算不到 9 GPU 小时，而且算一次可复用到很多实验。对真实预训练 pipeline 来说，这比训练一堆 proxy model 更容易落地。

量级上，这不是只在某个小 benchmark 上做微调的增量，而是一个值得进入数据配方工具箱的候选方向。
summary.technical_approach:
方法叫 WebGraphMix。核心设计很朴素：先在 Common Crawl 的 host-level hyperlink graph 上给每个 host 算结构中心性分数，再把属于这些 host 的文档映射回预训练语料，最后按 central / peripheral 的比例构造训练 mixture。

图的定义是 host 级而不是 page 级。每个节点是一个 host，例如 wikipedia.org；有向边表示 host 间超链接。作者用的是 Common Crawl 的 host graph，规模 13.9M nodes、439.6M directed edges。之所以选 host-level，而不是 page-level，一是规模可控，二是 host 级位置更稳定，也更适合和大规模语料中的文档来源对齐。

中心性主要试了两类：Betweenness centrality 和 Katz centrality。Betweenness 强调一个节点是否位于大量最短路径上，适合刻画“桥接不同社区”的 host；Katz centrality 则考虑来自邻居及更远节点的影响衰减，偏向刻画全局连接中的重要性。作者也试了 PageRank，但没有看到提升，这一点和 DCLM 里 PageRank 信号效果一般的观察一致。这个负结果其实很有信息量：对预训练数据来说，‘被很多节点指向’未必等于‘提供更有用的学习信号’，而桥接性和结构位置可能更关键。

拿到中心性分数后，作者把语料按 host 分桶，构造几种 mixture：只采 central、只采 peripheral、以及 central/peripheral 的混合，尤其关注 50/50 这种简单配比。这里的关键不是做复杂的连续权重优化，而是先用可解释的结构分区，观察能力变化方向。

更有意思的是它和内容质量信号的结合方式。论文把 centrality 与 DCLM-fasttext 质量分类器做 multiplicative 和 divisive 组合打分。虽然全文细节公式需要结合方法节看，但直觉上是在问：如果一个文档既来自结构中心 host，又被内容分类器判为高质量，是否更值得采样；反过来，是否可以通过除法或重加权避免某一类信号完全主导。实验结果表明这种组合优于单独使用任一信号，说明 web graph topology 与文本内容质量确实捕捉到不同维度。

从方法取舍看，这篇工作刻意避免训练额外模型，也不做下游驱动的 mixture search。优点是轻、稳、可迁移；代价是 centrality 只是 host 级粗粒度信号，无法区分同一 host 内部页面质量差异，也可能把大型聚合站点的结构优势和真实文本价值混在一起。
summary.experiments:
实验设置比较扎实，且控制得干净。作者把 WebGraphMix 接进标准化的 DCLM pipeline，训练了 400M 和 1B 两个规模的模型，分别用 8B 和 28B tokens。tokenizer、shuffle、优化器、训练流程都保持一致，尽量把变量压到“数据选择”本身。评测用的是 DCLM CORE v2 的 23 个任务，覆盖较广。

关键结果有几组。

1. 单独看 central vs peripheral 的能力偏置：
在 1B 模型上，采样结构更中心的 host 文档，相比 uniform sampling，在 Symbolic & Algorithmic Reasoning 上提升 +1.4%。而采样更边缘的 host，则在 Science & Factual Knowledge 和 Commonsense & Reasoning 上更好。这个结果很重要，因为它说明图位置不是单调的‘越中心越好’，而是不同区域承载不同能力相关信号。

2. mixture 优于单边采样：
用 betweenness centrality 做 50% central + 50% peripheral 的混合，在 23 个任务平均分上达到 41.4%，而 uniform sampling 是 39.8%。这是 +1.6 个点的平均提升。对预训练数据配方来说，这个幅度不小，尤其考虑到方法几乎不增加训练时成本。

3. 与内容质量信号结合进一步提升：
把 centrality 和 DCLM-fasttext 质量分类器结合后，平均分提升到 43.8%。也就是说，相比 uniform 的 39.8%，总提升达到 +4.0 个点；相比只用 graph mixture 的 41.4%，还有 +2.4 个点增益。这是全文最关键的结果之一，因为它直接支持“图结构信号与内容质量信号大体互补”。

4. 计算成本：
完整 Common Crawl host graph 的 centrality 计算总共不到 9 GPU 小时。这个数字很关键，它说明方法不是理论上可行、工程上很重，而是真的可以作为预训练前处理步骤。

如果看消融，最值得注意的不是某个 centrality 指标谁赢得更多，而是三件事：PageRank 无明显收益；betweenness 的解释性更强且效果稳定；central/peripheral 的混合优于只押一边。它们共同说明，图结构信号的价值在于提供能力互补的数据子集，而不是简单排序出一批‘最好网页’。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇值得精读。建议先看 Introduction 前三段和方法总览，抓住作者的核心假设：中心 host 暴露可复用抽象，边缘 host 保留长尾知识。然后直接看方法节里 graph construction、betweenness/Katz 定义、以及如何把 host score 映射回文档采样。这里要特别注意作者为什么选 host-level graph，以及为什么不把问题做成训练一个 document scorer。

实验部分建议按下面顺序读：
1. 主结果表：uniform、central-only、peripheral-only、50/50 mixture、与 fasttext 结合的结果。
2. 各能力子类结果：尤其是 Symbolic & Algorithmic、Science & Factual、Commonsense 三类，最能体现能力偏置。
3. centrality 指标对比和 PageRank 负结果。
4. 计算成本与可扩展性说明。

精读时有几个值得深挖的点。第一，host centrality 到 document utility 的映射是否过粗，未来是否应做 page-level 或 host-within-page hybrid。第二，central/peripheral 的最优比例是否随模型规模、token budget、训练阶段变化，是否可以做 curriculum 或 annealing。第三，图结构信号是否能和去重、质量过滤、domain mixture 一起形成更系统的数据配方，而不是单独使用。第四，中心 host 提升符号推理这一现象，究竟来自更强的模板复用、更多教程型文本，还是更高的跨域连接性；这值得后续做更细的机制分析。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a concrete gap in pretraining data selection. Most existing pipelines treat documents as independent units and rely on content-based quality filters, domain classifiers, or mixture optimization. They largely ignore the fact that the web is a graph. The central question here is whether a document's structural position in the hyperlink graph correlates with the kind of knowledge it contributes during pretraining, and whether that signal can be used for data selection without labels, auxiliary models, or downstream-driven search.
summary_en.importance:
This is a meaningful pretraining paper. Its contribution is not a more elaborate scorer, but a new selection axis: web-graph position. That matters for three reasons.

First, it provides a signal that appears complementary to content quality. When graph centrality is combined with the DCLM-fasttext quality classifier, performance improves beyond either signal alone. That suggests topology is not just a noisy proxy for existing quality scores.

Second, it sharpens the discussion around data mixtures and capability allocation. Central hosts seem to favor reusable abstractions and bridge-like information, while peripheral hosts contribute long-tail and specialized knowledge. The result is not 'higher quality is better' in a generic sense, but 'different structural regions induce different capability trade-offs.'

Third, the method is lightweight enough to matter in practice. Computing centrality on a 13.9M-node, 439.6M-edge host graph takes under 9 GPU hours and can be reused across many training runs. That is a much lower barrier than training multiple proxy models.

Overall, this looks like a credible addition to the pretraining data toolbox rather than a narrow benchmark trick.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The method, WebGraphMix, is simple by design. It computes structural centrality scores on the Common Crawl host-level hyperlink graph, maps those host scores back to documents in the pretraining corpus, and constructs mixtures that emphasize central hosts, peripheral hosts, or combinations of the two.

The graph is defined at the host level rather than the page level. Each node is a host such as wikipedia.org, and each directed edge indicates that one host links to another. The graph contains 13.9 million nodes and 439.6 million edges. This choice is important: host-level graphs are much more tractable than page-level graphs, and host identity aligns naturally with large-scale corpus provenance.

The paper mainly studies betweenness centrality and Katz centrality. Betweenness captures whether a host lies on many shortest paths and therefore acts as a bridge across otherwise weakly connected regions. Katz centrality measures global influence with distance decay. The authors also tried PageRank but did not observe gains, which is itself informative. For pretraining, being heavily linked may not be the same as providing broadly useful learning signals; bridge structure may matter more than raw popularity.

Once centrality scores are computed, documents are partitioned by host score and sampled into different mixtures: central-only, peripheral-only, and mixed settings such as 50/50. The point is not to solve a continuous optimization problem, but to create interpretable structural slices and observe how they affect learned capabilities.

A particularly useful part of the paper is the combination with content-based quality signals. The authors combine centrality with the DCLM-fasttext quality classifier using multiplicative and divisive scoring. The exact formulas matter less than the design intent: reward documents that are strong under both signals, while preventing one signal from completely dominating the other. The gains from this combination indicate that graph topology and textual quality capture different aspects of pretraining value.

The trade-off is clear. The method is cheap, unsupervised, and portable, but host-level centrality is coarse. It cannot distinguish high-value and low-value pages within the same host, and it may conflate structural prominence with actual textual usefulness for large aggregator sites.
summary_en.experiments:
The experimental setup is strong and well controlled. WebGraphMix is integrated into the standardized DCLM pipeline. Models are trained at 400M and 1B scales with 8B and 28B tokens respectively. Tokenization, shuffling, optimization, and training procedures are held fixed so that the main variable is data selection. Evaluation uses the 23-task DCLM CORE v2 benchmark.

Several results stand out.

1. Central and peripheral regions favor different capabilities.
At 1B scale, sampling from structurally central hosts improves Symbolic and Algorithmic Reasoning by +1.4% over uniform sampling. In contrast, sampling from peripheral hosts improves Science and Factual Knowledge as well as Commonsense and Reasoning. This is one of the paper's most important findings: graph position is not a monotonic quality ranking. Different parts of the web graph support different capability profiles.

2. Mixed sampling beats one-sided selection.
Using betweenness centrality, a 50% central plus 50% peripheral mixture reaches 41.4% average across the 23 tasks, compared with 39.8% for uniform sampling. A +1.6 point average gain is substantial for a data-selection intervention with almost no training-time overhead.

3. Graph structure and content quality are complementary.
Combining centrality with the DCLM-fasttext quality classifier raises the average to 43.8%. That is +4.0 points over uniform sampling and +2.4 points over the graph-only 50/50 mixture. This is the strongest evidence that topology provides information largely orthogonal to content-based quality scoring.

4. The preprocessing cost is low.
Computing centrality over the full host graph takes fewer than 9 GPU hours in total. This matters because it makes the method operationally plausible for real pretraining pipelines.

The most informative ablations are not about tiny differences between centrality metrics. They are: PageRank does not help, betweenness is stable and interpretable, and central-peripheral mixtures outperform either extreme alone. Together these results suggest that graph structure is useful because it exposes complementary data regions, not because it identifies a single best subset.
summary_en.reading_guide:
This one is worth a careful read. Start with the introduction and the method overview to lock in the main hypothesis: central hosts expose reusable abstractions, while peripheral hosts preserve long-tail knowledge. Then read the graph construction details, the definitions of betweenness and Katz centrality, and the mapping from host scores to document sampling. Pay attention to why the paper chooses host-level structure and why it avoids training a document scorer.

For the experiments, read in this order: the main comparison table with uniform, central-only, peripheral-only, 50/50 mixtures, and the combined graph-plus-fasttext results; then the capability breakdowns, especially Symbolic and Algorithmic, Science and Factual, and Commonsense; then the centrality-metric comparison including the negative PageRank result; and finally the compute-cost discussion.

A few deeper questions are worth carrying through the paper. Is host-level centrality too coarse, and would page-level or hybrid scoring work better? Does the best central-peripheral ratio change with model size, token budget, or training stage, suggesting a curriculum or annealing schedule? Can graph structure be integrated with deduplication, quality filtering, and domain mixtures into a more systematic recipe? And why exactly do central hosts help symbolic reasoning: because of more tutorial-style text, more reusable templates, or stronger cross-domain connectivity? Those are good follow-up directions.

recommendation.zh: 这篇会直接影响你做 web-scale mixture 的先验：先看它是否在固定 token budget 下稳定优于 learned scorer，再决定要不要把图结构信号接进内部数据管线。
recommendation.en: This can change your prior on web-scale mixture design: first check whether graph centrality beats learned scorers under fixed token budgets, then decide if structural signals belong in your data pipeline.

paper.title: Repetition Mismatch: Why Data Mixture Experiments Don't Scale and How to Fix Them
paper.abstract: Pre-training data mixtures are commonly tuned by running small-scale experiments and extrapolating to the target training budget. When high-quality data is scarce and must be repeated, this extrapolation frequently fails, but the source of the failure has not been isolated. We show that a primary culprit is a repetition mismatch: because high-quality datasets are small, their repetition rate changes as the training budget grows, shifting the optimal mixture in ways that small-scale proxy experim

summary.core_problem: 解决预训练数据配比实验在从小规模代理实验外推到目标训练预算时经常失效的问题，尤其是在高质量小数据集必须被重复采样的场景下。
summary.importance: 这是很实在的 pretrain 方法论文。贡献不是又画一条 scaling 曲线，而是隔离出一个长期被混在一起的混杂因素：repetition mismatch。它直接影响数据混合实验的可迁移性、compute 使用效率，以及高质量稀缺数据在大训练预算下的最优占比判断。
summary.technical_approach: 作者指出，小规模 mixture sweep 之所以不能可靠外推，一个主要原因是高质量小数据集在不同训练 horizon 下的重复率会变化，导致最优 mixture 随预算漂移。为控制这个变量，论文提出 repetition-controlled subsampling：在小规模代理实验中对子数据集做抽样，使其重复率与目标预算下保持一致。这样可以用单个低成本实验更准确地预测目标预算下的最优配比。
summary.experiments: 在一个 two-source 设置中，将有限高质量数据与 web crawl 混合，在 757M 参数模型上，只用目标 token 数的 1/16 做一次 repetition-controlled 实验，就能把 mixture 预测误差控制在距最优 0.05 以内；若不控制 repetition，误差达到 0.75。要达到相近精度，不做控制需要跑 3-4 个 horizon，计算成本高得多。这个 setup 虽然简化，但足够干净，能把 repetition 变量单独拎出来。
summary.authors_note: 作者包含 Marek Rei。若无论文首页机构信息，不宜进一步补充。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses why pretraining data-mixture experiments often fail to extrapolate from small proxy runs to the target training budget, especially when scarce high-quality data must be repeated.
summary_en.importance: This is a genuinely useful pretraining-method paper. The contribution is not another generic scaling plot; it isolates a confound that has often been mixed into data-mixture tuning: repetition mismatch. That directly affects mixture transferability, compute efficiency, and how one should reason about the optimal share of scarce high-quality data at larger budgets.
summary_en.technical_approach: The authors argue that small-scale mixture sweeps fail mainly because the repetition rate of small high-quality datasets changes with training horizon, causing the optimal mixture to drift with budget.
